titulo: The evening that starts late and ends with one bill
subtitulo: Which table, what is on it, who pays for the round, and how to leave without ending the night
cena: Half past ten, a table out on the pavement, small glasses and small plates arriving, and someone else already deciding who pays.
frasePiso: One table, one bill, and you know both what is on it and how to stand up from it.
decisao: em que mesa me ponho e quanto custa a noite; a rodada, quem paga, e como me despeço da mesa sem encerrar a noite dos outros

fatosDatados.afirmacao: In Greece a cover charge is prohibited, and no product — bread and bottled water included — may be served and billed without prior consent, with a fine of €500 per item. Bread may be charged as an item if it is offered and accepted. The price list is compulsory, in Greek, visible at the entrance and again before you order, with VAT included: €1,000 for a missing list and €500 for any item billed above the listed price.
fatosDatados.fonte: Art. 72 dos Κανόνες ΔΙ.Ε.Π.Π.Υ. (ΥΑ 91354/2017, ΦΕΚ Β΄2983/30.8.2017) proíbe cobrar κουβέρ, e nenhum produto — incluindo pão e água engarrafada — pode ser servido e cobrado sem consentimento prévio. Multa de €500 por item. Transparência de preço, arts. 70–71: lista obrigatória, em grego, visível na entrada E antes do pedido, preços com IVA; multa de €1.000 pela ausência de lista e €500 por item cobrado acima do listado.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Tipping in Greece is institutionally recognised, but only as a tax matter: law 5162/2024 exempts tips of up to €300 a month per worker from income tax, for amounts paid from 01.11.2024, and exempts the whole of it from social contributions. That confirms tipping exists. It confirms no percentage whatsoever.
fatosDatados.fonte: Gorjeta tem fonte institucional, mas só para o tratamento FISCAL: o ν.5162/2024 isenta de imposto gorjetas até €300/mês por trabalhador, para valores pagos a partir de 01.11.2024, e isenta de contribuição social o total. Isso confirma que a gorjeta existe e é reconhecida — não confirma percentual nenhum.

steps.pt: The evening here starts later than yours and moves slower. Nobody is waiting for you to finish your glass.
You order for the table, not for yourself. Small glasses, small plates, and the night assembles itself.
Good evening! Outside or inside?

steps.promptPt: The pavement tables are still empty and the room is loud. Say which side you want. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a table outside?
Nothing may be served and billed without being offered first. Bread and bottled water are included in that.

steps.promptPt: A basket lands on the table before you have ordered anything. Ask the one question that settles it. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is the bread charged?

steps.es: Ένα ευρώ το άτομο. Το θέλετε;
steps.pt: One euro a head. Do you want it?
steps.tts: Ένα ευρώ το άτομο. Το θέλετε;
steps.acao: That second half is the law working. Say yes or say no — both are complete answers here.

steps.promptPt: The first round of the evening, and you want the aniseed one that comes with ice and water. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'd like an ouzo, please.

steps.promptPt: The shelf behind the bar has bottles with no labels you recognise. Open the door to those. Speak now.
steps.pt: What do you have that's local?

steps.es: Έχουμε ρακόμελο, τσίπουρο και ούζο από τη Λέσβο.
steps.pt: We have rakomelo, tsipouro and ouzo from Lesbos.
steps.tts: Έχουμε ρακόμελο, τσίπουρο και ούζο από τη Λέσβο.
steps.acao: Three names and one island. Pick by the island if the drink means nothing to you yet.

steps.pt: The price list on the wall is in Greek, at the door and again before you order. It is an obligation, not decor.

steps.promptPt: Four glasses are up, four people are looking at you, and nobody has drunk yet. Speak now.
steps.pt: Cheers! (to our health)
The toast is short and it is said to faces, not to the ceiling. Glasses meet, eyes meet, then you drink.

steps.promptPt: The second round has just been ordered and you want it on your side of the table. Speak now.
steps.pt: This one's on me.

steps.es: Όχι, όχι! Σήμερα κερνάω εγώ. Την άλλη φορά εσύ.
steps.pt: No, no! Today it's on me. Next time it's you.
steps.tts: Όχι, όχι! Σήμερα κερνάω εγώ. Την άλλη φορά εσύ.
steps.acao: Do not push back twice. Thank him and take the next one — that is the whole arrangement.

steps.pt: One person pays for the table and the next round belongs to somebody else. It gets remembered, not settled.

steps.promptPt: Your glass is empty, the plates are still half full, and the table is nowhere near going home. Speak now.
steps.pt: Another one, please.

steps.promptPt: Six things came to the table over two hours and you want one number for the lot. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much is it all together?
Tips are real here and legally recognised. No percentage is standard, so rounding up is a complete answer.

steps.promptPt: The bill is on a saucer in front of you and there are eleven euros in your pocket. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I pay by card?
Of course. Do you want a receipt?
Leaving is announced, not performed. You say you are going, you say goodnight, and then you actually go.

steps.promptPt: It is one in the morning, the table is staying, and you have a ferry at seven. Stand up and say it. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'm off. Goodnight!

steps.promptPt: The table is already planning the next night while you are still standing up. Leave the door open. Speak now.
steps.pt: See you tomorrow.

steps.es: Έχετε τραπέζι έξω; Γεια μας! Πόσο κάνει όλα μαζί; Τα λέμε αύριο.
steps.pinyin: E-he-te tra-PE-zi E-kso. YA mas. PO-so KA-ni O-la ma-ZEE. ta LE-me AV-ri-o
steps.pt: Shadow the four sentences that carry an entire evening from the pavement to the door.
steps.tts: Έχετε τραπέζι έξω; Γεια μας! Πόσο κάνει όλα μαζί; Τα λέμε αύριο.

steps.pt: I04 done. A table outside, a local glass, one bill, and a goodnight that keeps the table open for you.

aprofundar.titulo: One table, one bill, one goodnight

secoes.corpo: Drinks arrive small and food arrives in the middle. Nobody is guarding a plate, and the plate you were given is not a portion assigned to you. Ordering two or three things and pushing them into the centre is the ordinary move, and it is also the cheapest way to try five things instead of committing to one.

exemplos.pt: What do you have that's local?

secoes.titulo: The bread question, and why it is a question
secoes.corpo: A cover charge is prohibited outright, and no item may be served and billed without prior consent — bread and bottled water named explicitly, with a fine of €500 per item. Bread can perfectly well be charged if it was offered and you took it. So the useful sentence is not a complaint, it is a question asked in three words before the basket is opened.

Prices have to be listed in Greek, visible at the entrance and again before you order, VAT included. A missing list carries a €1,000 fine and an item billed above the listed price carries €500. You do not need to argue with anything: reading the board on the way in tells you what the evening costs before you sit down.

One person pays for the table. Trying to divide the bill mid-evening tends to be waved away, not because anyone is being extravagant but because the round is the unit and the next one is somebody else's. Saying κερνάω εγώ early is a gesture; producing a calculator at one in the morning is arithmetic on the pavement.

Tips are recognised in Greek tax law — up to €300 a month per worker is exempt from income tax — which tells you they exist and are normal. It tells you nothing about how much. There is no defensible national percentage, and rounding the bill up or leaving the coins is a complete answer everywhere.

permissao: You are allowed to sit at a table for three hours and order twice. Nobody is counting your glasses, nobody needs the table back, and the waiter who has not come over is not ignoring you — he is leaving you alone, which is the same gesture done the other way round. And when somebody insists on paying, you are allowed to simply say thank you and take the next round instead of fighting over a bill.
espelho: Anyone who has ever been in a group where one person quietly gets the round in already knows the arrangement — it works on memory rather than arithmetic, and it only feels strange when you are the newest person at the table. The only new part is that here the memory runs to tomorrow night rather than to next month.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You reach for your share and your money is pushed back across the table, twice, with some force.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: He is being extravagant, or he thinks I cannot afford it.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The round, not the individual drink, is the unit that gets paid for. One person covers the table and the next occasion belongs to someone else. Refusing the offer twice reads as declining the arrangement rather than as good manners.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say thank you, put the money away, and get the next round in before anyone else moves — that is the second half of the same gesture, and it is what makes the first half work.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The evening stops having an accounting layer running underneath it, and you get invited to the one after this one.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: This is an observed pattern of hospitality, not a rule. Younger groups and mixed tables split perfectly happily, and if the table is dividing it up on a phone, divide it up on a phone.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Bread, and then a small dish nobody asked for, arrive at the table before you have ordered.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This will show up on the bill and there will be nothing I can do about it.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A cover charge is prohibited, and no product may be served and billed without prior consent — bread and bottled water named explicitly, at €500 per item. Bread is lawfully charged only when it was offered and accepted, which is why waiters here often ask.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask before the basket is opened, in three words, and read the price list at the entrance on the way in. Both are ordinary moves, and neither of them is a confrontation.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop bracing for the end of the meal, and the small dish that really was a gift stays a gift.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not every extra plate is a charge. Something sent over at the end of the evening is very often exactly what it looks like, and treating it as a line item is the one way to get it wrong.
